title: Application Logging

richText: Record application events
A log records an application event, warning, or failure.
Your Java code calls the SLF4J logging API. A logging implementation writes those messages.
Boot’s standard logging starter uses Logback as the default implementation.
Logs go to the console by default. File logging requires configuration.
Choose a log level

1: An unexpected condition that the application can handle.
A failed operation that needs attention.

richText: A logger’s configured level is a threshold. INFO allows INFO, WARN, and ERROR, while filtering DEBUG and TRACE.
Write messages with a logger

example.title: Write startup messages at different levels
description: Run this application with the default INFO logging level.
Boot also writes its own startup messages.
explanation: LoggerFactory creates a logger named for this class.
CommandLineRunner runs after Spring has started the application.
The INFO, WARN, and ERROR calls are written. The DEBUG call is filtered out.
Timestamps, thread names, and other prefixes depend on the logging format.

richText: Configure levels and destinations
logging.level.root sets the default level. logging.level followed by a package name sets that package’s level.
Use package-level DEBUG when investigating one part of the application.
logging.file.name adds a log file. Console logging continues.
logging.pattern.console controls the console format.
Use logback-spring.xml when you need Logback appenders, filters, or Boot-specific profile configuration. An appender chooses where messages are written.

example.title: Set package logging and write to a file
description: The application classes are in the com.example package.
explanation: DEBUG is enabled for com.example while other packages keep INFO.
app.log is written relative to the application’s working directory.
The console pattern prints the timestamp and message.
Profile-specific configuration can choose different levels for development and production.

richText: Make logs useful
Use SLF4J {} placeholders instead of building messages with string concatenation.
Pass a caught exception as the throwable argument when its stack trace is needed.
Logging an exception does not propagate it to the caller.
Use a correlation ID to connect messages from the same request or background operation.
Log the operation and a safe identifier. Keep passwords, tokens, and private message bodies out of logs.
Avoid global DEBUG during normal production operation. It produces extra output and can expose sensitive values.
The Actuator loggers endpoint can inspect and change levels at runtime. Restrict access to it.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Mastering Logging in Spring Boot: A Complete Guide, from Logback to SLF4J

summary: Understand the logger, choose levels, and configure console and file output.
